hints: Sketch the two sides as $y=|x-2|$ and $y=2\sin(x/2)$ on the restricted interval $0<x<\pi$.
For the modulus graph mark its vertex at $x=2$; for the sine graph mark its passage through the origin and value $2$ at $x=\pi$.
Use the shapes and interval endpoints to show exactly one crossing, and state that each crossing corresponds to a root.
walkthrough:
Sketch the graph of $y_1 = |x - 2|$ on the interval $0 < x < \pi$:
$$\text{Vertex at } (2, 0) \text{ on the } x\text{-axis.}$$
$$\text{Left branch: } y = 2 - x \text{ with } y\text{-intercept } (0, 2), \text{ passing through } (1, 1).$$
$$\text{Right branch: } y = x - 2 \text{ ending at } (\pi, \pi - 2) \approx (3.14, 1.14).$$

Sketch the graph of $y_2 = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ on $0 < x < \pi$:
$$\text{Starts at the origin } (0, 0) \text{ since } 2\sin(0) = 0.$$
$$\text{At } x = 2: \quad y_2 = 2\sin(1) \approx 2(0.8415) = 1.683.$$
$$\text{Reaches its maximum at } x = \pi: \quad y_2 = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2(1) = 2.$$

Compare the two functions to demonstrate a single intersection:
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y_1 = 2 > y_2 = 0$$
$$\text{At } x = 2: \quad y_1 = 0 < y_2 = 1.683$$
$$\text{Because } y_1 \text{ is strictly decreasing on } [0, 2] \text{ and } y_2 \text{ is strictly increasing, they cross exactly once in } (0, 2).$$
$$\text{For } x \in [2, \pi): \quad y_1 = x - 2 \leqslant \pi - 2 \approx 1.14 < 1.683 \leqslant y_2, \text{ so they never cross for } x \geqslant 2.$$
$$\text{Hence there is exactly one root for } 0 < x < \pi.$$

hints: Evaluate $f(1)$ and $f(1.5)$ with enough digits to display opposite signs.
Since the function is continuous on $[1,1.5]$, use the sign change to locate the root strictly between the endpoints.
walkthrough:
Define the continuous function $f(x) = (2 - x) - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ for $x < 2$:
$$f(x) = 2 - x - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$$

State the conclusion using the intermediate value theorem:
$$\text{Since } f(1) > 0 \text{ and } f(1.5) < 0, \text{ and } f(x) \text{ is continuous on } [1, 1.5],$$
$$\text{there is a sign change. Hence the root lies between } 1 \text{ and } 1.5.$$

hints: Start with $x_1=1.03$, feed each output back into the formula, and record every iterate to 4 decimal places.
Continue through the alternating convergence until the iterates justify rounding the root to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Substitute the initial value $x_1 = 1.03$ into the iteration formula $x_{n+1} = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{x_n}{2}\right)$ in radian mode:
$$x_2 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.03}{2}\right) = 2 - 2\sin(0.515) = 2 - 2(0.492543) = 2 - 0.985087 \approx 1.0149$$

Calculate subsequent iterates to 4 decimal places:
$$x_3 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0149}{2}\right) = 2 - 2\sin(0.50745) = 2 - 2(0.485966) \approx 1.0281$$
$$x_4 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0281}{2}\right) = 2 - 2\sin(0.51405) = 2 - 2(0.491702) \approx 1.0166$$
$$x_5 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0166}{2}\right) = 2 - 2\sin(0.5083) = 2 - 2(0.486716) \approx 1.0266$$
$$x_6 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0266}{2}\right) \approx 1.0179$$
$$x_7 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0179}{2}\right) \approx 1.0255$$
$$x_8 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0255}{2}\right) \approx 1.0189$$
$$x_9 = 2 - 2\sin\left(\dfrac{1.0189}{2}\right) \approx 1.0246$$

Determine the root to 2 decimal places:
$$\text{Successive iterates oscillate within } (1.018, 1.025) \text{ and round to } 1.02:$$
$$x = 1.02$$
